what it does: Asks Kite for a live quote on every F&O contract in scope (about 27,400 contracts across 216 underlyings) and stores it raw. Also totals call and put OI and volume per underlying, and records the spot price.
when it runs: Every 15 minutes during a trading session, 20 seconds after each candle close: 09:30, 09:45 ... 15:30, plus one at 15:45 after the close. 26 readings a day. Sleeps through weekends and holidays.
how long it takes: 28 to 40 seconds a reading. Measured on 18 Sep: 9 readings, fastest 28.1s, slowest 40.1s, 56-57 Kite requests each.
what it needs: A valid Kite token; the NFO instrument list; the single-writer lock on db/derivatives.db.
what it produces: db/derivatives.db: snapshots (about 27,240 rows a reading), underlying_snapshots, contracts, captures.
what breaks if it stops: The tab freezes on the last reading it got. Those readings can never be recovered as live quotes - only rebuilt from candles, which carry no traded average price, so premium and the whole liquidity screen are lost for those hours for ever.

what it does: Turns each captured reading into the numbers the tab shows: OI build-up, volume against its own average, volume-to-OI, premium in rupees, PCR, max pain, futures basis, the unusual flags.
when it runs: Every 60 seconds, all day. Picks up any reading from the last 24 hours that has snapshots but no metrics, oldest first, up to 40 at a time.
how long it takes: 8 to 10 seconds per reading of about 10,000 contract rows (measured, logs/recompute_seeded.log, 19 Sep). A full 27,000-row reading should be roughly 25-30s - not verified.
what it needs: The capture loop to have written snapshots first. Write access to db/derivatives.db.
what it produces: db/derivatives.db: metrics - one row per contract per reading, plus one per underlying and expiry.
what breaks if it stops: Capture keeps running but the tab shows nothing new. Every block on the Derivative tab reads metrics, not snapshots.

what it does: Deletes rows older than the keep-windows, after first rolling each day being trimmed into a permanent daily summary.
when it runs: Once a calendar day, from inside the capture loop, only after the day last reading is done and never before 15:45.
how long it takes: Not yet measured - it has never had anything to delete. The store is three days old.
what it needs: The capture loop to be running. It refuses outright if a window would reach the session the tab is serving.
what it produces: Deletes from snapshots, metrics, candles_15m, underlying_snapshots. Writes daily_rollups.
what breaks if it stops: The store grows without limit: about 223 MB a trading day, roughly 55 GB in a year under the old windows, about 12.8 GB under the current ones.

what it does: Compresses a whole session of 15-minute rows for one contract into one row: open, high, low, close, volume, OI at open and close, premium.
when it runs: Automatically, inside the prune, for any day about to lose detail. Can also be run by hand for one date.
what it needs: snapshots or candles_15m for that day.
what it produces: db/derivatives.db: daily_rollups, kept for ever. Currently 0 rows.
what breaks if it stops: Pruning would destroy history instead of compressing it. Nothing on the tab reads daily_rollups today.

what it does: Downloads the exchange own 15-minute candles with open interest for the last 10 sessions, so a versus-its-own-average baseline exists on day one.
when it runs: By hand only. No schedule. Last full run 18 Sep 2026.
how long it takes: 2 hours 6 minutes for full scope. Measured: 917,981 rows, 15,098 contracts, 15,100 requests, 7,550 seconds, 2 contracts a second.
what it needs: A valid Kite token. Hours of Kite rate budget.
what it produces: db/derivatives.db: candles_15m (2.68 million rows, 329 MB), backfill_progress.
what breaks if it stops: New contracts have no history, so volume-against-its-own-average says no baseline instead of giving a number.

what it does: Downloads each in-scope futures contract own daily candles. A contract lives about three months, so one request covers its whole life.
when it runs: By hand only. No schedule.
how long it takes: One request per futures contract; a full run is about 432 requests. Not verified - it has never completed.
what breaks if it stops: Already broken. candles_day is EMPTY today - 0 rows, verified. That is why the Daily candles button on the futures chart is greyed out on every symbol. The only run on record, 19 Sep, returned 0 rows and 2 errors.

what it does: Rebuilds a past session 15-minute readings from the exchange candles when the live loop missed them. Marks every rebuilt row as candle-derived, never as a live quote.
when it runs: By hand only, after a session has closed.
how long it takes: About 90 seconds for one session. Measured 19 Sep: 165,692 rows over 17 readings for 10,628 contracts in 1 minute 33 seconds.
what it needs: candles_15m already backfilled for that session; a valid Kite token for the spot leg.
what it produces: db/derivatives.db: snapshots with source = kite.candles_15m and average_price left empty.
what breaks if it stops: A missed afternoon stays completely blank instead of partly recovered. Note what it rebuilds can never carry premium, and on 19 Sep the spot leg failed on every symbol because the Kite token was dead.

what it does: Keeps the ordinary stock price candles current for the rest of the app - Discover, the charts, the status chip.
when it runs: Every 300 seconds while the market is open; idles 1,800 seconds when closed.
how long it takes: 77 seconds a cycle, measured 20 Sep - but that cycle produced 0 rows and 210 errors because the Kite token was rejected.
what it needs: A valid Kite token; db/kanida.db read-only for the stock list.
what breaks if it stops: The Derivative tab is NOT affected - it reads none of this. The rest of the app goes stale.

what it does: Finds chart patterns for the Discover tab.
when it runs: Polls every 60 seconds.
what breaks if it stops: The Derivative tab is NOT affected - it never calls the scanner.

what it does: Logs in to Zerodha and mints a fresh access token. Lives in a different project on the Desktop, not in this repo.
when it runs: Windows Scheduled Task KanidaZerodhaAuth, every 30 minutes all week - but the script itself exits immediately outside 06:00-16:30 IST and does nothing at all on Saturday or Sunday.
what it produces: A row in the kite_tokens table of the Desktop project database.
what breaks if it stops: EVERYTHING that touches Kite stops: capture, backfill, seed, equity prices. This is the single point of failure for the whole pipeline, and it was failing when this was written - auto-auth ran but did not mint a new token, 20 Sep 07:08.

what it does: Serves the app and all 16 Derivative routes. Opens db/derivatives.db read-only.
when it runs: Runs continuously on port 8082. Started by hand with kanida-app/scripts/start-pilot.ps1.
what it needs: db/derivatives.db to read; var/pilot.sqlite3 for sign-in.
what it produces: The web pages and the JSON the tab draws with.
what breaks if it stops: The whole app is down.

what it does: Is there any F&O data, how fresh is it, what liquidity floors are in force.
when it runs: On demand. Nothing polls on a timer.
what breaks if it stops: The tab header cannot say how fresh the data is.

what it does: Did the capture actually work at this reading, and which fields are missing. Built after the outage that left the global status chip saying healthy.
when it runs: On demand - but NOTHING calls it yet. Server-side only, with tests.
what breaks if it stops: Nothing - it is not wired into the screen yet.

what it does: What can be filtered on, and the legal values for each.
when it runs: On demand, once when the tab opens.
what breaks if it stops: The filter builder cannot offer any choices.

what it does: The main market screen: one row per underlying with volume, OI, premium, build-up counts and the per-contract unusual evidence.
when it runs: On demand - when the tab opens, on a filter change, on refresh.
what it needs: A signed-in member; the metrics table populated.
what it produces: 390 KB of JSON. 378 KB of that is the rows, and 167 KB of the rows is the per-contract evidence added by the P06 fix.
what breaks if it stops: The main screen is empty and no other block has a symbol to follow.

what it does: The older, narrower unusual-activity list per underlying.
when it runs: On demand - but the tab no longer calls it. Superseded by the screener.
what breaks if it stops: Nothing today.

what it does: The option chain: calls, strike, puts, at one reading.
when it runs: On demand, when a symbol is chosen.
what breaks if it stops: The option chain block shows its empty state.

what it does: Open interest by strike, calls against puts.
when it runs: On demand.
what breaks if it stops: The OI-by-strike block shows its empty state.

what it does: Ten small series - the at-the-money call and the four strikes above it, the at-the-money put and the four below - showing OI added or removed since the previous close.
when it runs: On demand.
what breaks if it stops: The delta-OI grid empties, and the IV grid empties with it - the IV tiles get their ten contracts from this route.

what it does: The index overview list.
when it runs: On demand.
what breaks if it stops: The index panel empties, and the tab loses its fallback symbol.

what it does: The cross-market futures list.
when it runs: On demand.
what breaks if it stops: The futures list empties.

what it does: The front futures contract own candles for the price chart.
when it runs: On demand, and again when the reader switches 15-minute to daily.
how long it takes: 624 ms for 15-minute. 0.6 ms for daily, because daily is empty.
what it needs: A signed-in member; an underlying that has a futures contract.
what breaks if it stops: The price chart at the top of the tab goes blank. This is the slowest route on the tab by a factor of four.

what it does: One contract price and OI through the session, or the underlying spot and total OI.
when it runs: On demand, when a strike or tile is clicked.
what breaks if it stops: The linked panel beside the chart empties.

what it does: Put-call ratio by OI and by volume at every reading of the session.
when it runs: On demand.
what breaks if it stops: The PCR block empties.

what it does: The max-pain strike and the spot beside it at every reading.
when it runs: On demand.
what breaks if it stops: The max-pain block empties.

what it does: Implied volatility through the session. The ONLY number on the tab that is calculated rather than captured - Kite does not supply it.
when it runs: On demand. Called once for the block, plus once per tile in the 2x5 IV grid - so up to 11 calls for one symbol.
what it needs: A signed-in member; an underlying; a spot price at that reading.
what breaks if it stops: The IV block and the ten IV tiles empty.

what it does: Front futures OI against its own average, and the basis, through the session.
when it runs: On demand.
what breaks if it stops: The futures build-up block empties.

what it does: One row per F&O contract ever seen: symbol, underlying, call or put or future, strike, expiry, lot size.
when it runs: Refreshed by the capture loop when it resolves scope.
what it needs: Grows as new expiries list. Old rows are never deleted.
what breaks if it stops: The tab cannot name a strike or an expiry.

what it does: One row per contract per 15-minute reading: last price, the day traded average price, volume, open interest. The raw record.
when it runs: Written by the capture loop at every reading.
what it needs: About 74 MB a trading day at full scope.
what it produces: 427,031 rows, 85 MB plus a 21 MB retired index, kept 30 days.
what breaks if it stops: Nothing can be recomputed. The raw input is gone.

what it does: One row per contract per reading and one per underlying-and-expiry, holding every number the tab prints.
when it runs: Written by the metrics loop, within a minute of each capture.
what it produces: 438,213 rows, 121 MB plus 80 MB of indexes, kept 90 days.
what breaks if it stops: The Derivative tab goes blank. This is the table it actually reads.

what it does: The exchange own 15-minute bars with open interest, per contract. The history the versus-its-own-average baselines stand on.
when it runs: Written by the backfill.
what it produces: 2,675,883 rows over 14 sessions (31 Aug to 18 Sep), 329 MB plus an 83 MB index, kept 180 days.
what breaks if it stops: All unusual-volume baselines fall back to no baseline.

what it does: Each futures contract own daily bars.
when it runs: Written by the daily backfill.
what breaks if it stops: Already broken: the Daily candles toggle on the futures chart is dead on every symbol.

what it does: One row per underlying per reading: spot, front futures price, total call and put OI and volume.
when it runs: Written by the capture loop at every reading.
what it needs: About 5,600 rows a day, under 1 MB.
what breaks if it stops: The index overview panel loses its spot and totals. NOTE: another worker is adding a spot_source column here right now.

what it does: One row per contract per session - the permanent summary that survives the prune.
when it runs: Written by the prune, and by the rollup command.
what it needs: Only written when a prune happens.
what breaks if it stops: History is deleted instead of compressed when the prune finally runs.

what it does: One row per 15-minute reading: did it run, how many rows, how many requests, how many seconds, how late. The run ledger.
when it runs: Written twice per reading - at the start and at the end.
what it produces: 26 rows (18 Sep only), under 0.1 MB, kept for ever.
what breaks if it stops: The loop loses its memory of what it has already done and could double-capture or skip.

what it does: One row per contract per backfill window - what was already fetched, so a rerun resumes instead of starting over.
when it runs: Written during a backfill.
what breaks if it stops: A rerun of the backfill refetches everything from scratch - another two hours of Kite budget.

what it does: One row per backfill, seed or prune run.
when it runs: Written at the start and end of each such run.
what it produces: 13 rows, under 0.1 MB, kept for ever.
what breaks if it stops: No record of what was rebuilt when.

what it does: Three settings: when scope was resolved, the scope counts, the newest live reading.
when it runs: Written by the capture loop.
what it produces: 3 rows, under 0.1 MB, kept for ever.
what breaks if it stops: The tab loses its pointer to the newest real reading.

what it does: The only store the Derivative tab reads. 664 MB on disk plus a 615 MB write-ahead log - about 1.3 GB in total today, for three sessions of data.
when it runs: Read on every request; written by the capture and metrics loops.
what it needs: SQLite in WAL mode; the advisory writer-lock file beside it.
what breaks if it stops: The whole tab goes to: No F&O data captured yet.

what it does: The advisory lock that stops two writers colliding. The capture command takes it; the metrics loop does NOT - it relies on a 60-second SQLite busy timeout instead.
when it runs: Held while a capture command runs.
what breaks if it stops: Two writers could collide. In practice SQLite blocks rather than corrupts, but a long prune could stall a metrics pass.

what it does: A local copy of the Kite NFO instrument dump, so scope can be resolved without refetching.
when it runs: Refreshed when scope is resolved.
what breaks if it stops: Scope resolution needs a fresh Kite call every time.

what it does: The ordinary stock-price store, 18.2 GB. Feeds Discover, the charts and the status chip.
when it runs: Written every 5 minutes by the equity loop.
what breaks if it stops: NOT read by the Derivative tab. The rest of the app goes stale. NOTE: another worker may start reading it here, to recover missing spot prices.

what it does: The old 147 GB engine store. Last received a price on 31 Jul 2026. Kept alive mainly for a 0.2 MB table of stock names and sectors.
when it runs: Read-only, occasionally.
what breaks if it stops: NOT read by the Derivative tab. Company names elsewhere in the app go missing.

what it does: The app own small database: users, sign-in sessions, invites, plans, watchlists. 1.3 MB.
when it runs: Read on every request.
what breaks if it stops: Nobody can sign in, so every Derivative route answers not-a-member. The data is fine but unreachable.

what it does: A cache of the last good answer for the Discover reads, so the app can show the last scan while the scanner restarts.
what breaks if it stops: NOT used by the Derivative tab - the derivative routes deliberately do not cache.

what it does: Offline price-movement history for two chart patterns. 175 MB.
what breaks if it stops: NOT used by the Derivative tab.

what it does: Per-strategy counts for the Discover tab, rebuilt by a background thread inside the server every 30 minutes. 154 MB.
what breaks if it stops: NOT used by the Derivative tab.

what it does: The capture loop own log - the only place a missed reading shows up early.
when it runs: Appended at every reading.
what breaks if it stops: Nothing watches this file. A dead loop is invisible until someone opens the tab and notices the clock has stopped.
